question.text: A bear put spread with 83 put (bought at 0.07) and 82.50 put (sold at 0.05) has a maximum profit of:

explanation.text: The Logic: Max profit = Strike difference - Net premium = (83 - 82.50) - (0.07 - 0.05) = 0.50 - 0.02 = Rs. 0.48. Occurs when USDINR is at or below 82.50 (both options exercised). The Trap: Max LOSS = Net premium = Rs. 0.02. BEP = 83 - 0.02 = 82.98. Note: This is a limited-risk, limited-reward bearish strategy. Source: NISM-Series-I Currency Derivatives workbook, pp.106-107.
